description: Example Confluence CQL conformance manifest with fake values; copy outside the repository and replace values before live use.

cases.description: Proves Confluence accepts explicit space equality and page type clauses emitted through the broker.
Proves Confluence accepts the broker-emitted space IN list form.
Proves Confluence accepts title and text contains clauses with escaped string literal content.
Proves Confluence accepts label equality and inequality clauses.
Proves Confluence accepts label list inclusion and exclusion clauses.
cases.cql: label IN (runbook, deploy) AND label NOT IN (obsolete)

cases.description: Proves Confluence accepts creator equality and inequality account-id clauses.
Proves Confluence accepts creator list inclusion and exclusion account-id clauses.
cases.cql: creator IN ("account-id-one", "account-id-two") AND creator NOT IN ("account-id-three")

cases.description: Proves Confluence accepts contributor equality and inequality account-id clauses.
Proves Confluence accepts contributor list inclusion and exclusion account-id clauses.
cases.cql: contributor IN ("account-id-one", "account-id-two") AND contributor NOT IN ("account-id-three")

cases.description: Proves Confluence accepts mention equality and list account-id clauses.
Proves Confluence accepts page id and content.id equality and list clauses.
cases.cql: id = 123456 AND id IN (123456, 234567) AND content.id = 123456 AND content.id IN (123456, 234567)

cases.description: Proves Confluence accepts ancestor equality/list clauses and parent equality clauses.
cases.cql: ancestor = 123456 AND ancestor IN (123456, 234567) AND parent = 123456

cases.description: Tracks Atlassian-published parent IN syntax that may fail on current Confluence Cloud search endpoints.

expect.expectedUpstreamFailure: Atlassian publishes parent IN, but current Confluence Cloud /wiki/rest/api/content/search endpoints may return an upstream error for this syntax.

cases.description: Proves Confluence accepts all broker-supported created date comparison operators.
cases.cql: created = 2024-01-31 AND created != 2024-02-01 AND created < 2024-12-31 AND created <= 2024-12-31 AND created > 2024-01-01 AND created >= 2024-01-01

cases.description: Proves Confluence accepts all broker-supported lastModified date comparison operators.
cases.cql: lastModified = 2024-01-31 AND lastModified != 2024-02-01 AND lastModified < 2024-12-31 AND lastModified <= 2024-12-31 AND lastModified > 2024-01-01 AND lastModified >= 2024-01-01

cases.description: Proves Confluence accepts created ordering after broker composition.
Proves Confluence accepts descending lastModified ordering after broker composition.
Proves Confluence accepts title ordering with the broker's default direction emission.
Proves Confluence accepts supported multi-field ordering after broker composition.
cases.cql: title ~ "runbook" ORDER BY lastModified DESC, title
